text:
TSMC's Three CPO Paths: The Physics of Bandwidth Multiplication and the Engineering of Yield Division

TSMC($TSM )'s accelerated push into co-packaged optics can be quantified along three parallel expansion paths: raising per-lane speed from 200 Gbps toward 400 Gbps and beyond, widening optical channel count from 16 to 32, 64, and beyond, and introducing wavelength-division multiplexing so a single fiber carries multiple wavelengths simultaneously. If all three advance in tandem, the bandwidth curve doubles roughly every two years — from a 3.2 Tbps baseline today toward a theoretical 128x by 2040, implying a path into the hundreds of terabits.

Those numbers deserve scrutiny, but the more useful question is why the CPO bandwidth curve can exhibit this kind of regularity — and what constrains it from translating into production output on the roadmap's cadence.

The physics behind the bandwidth wall
The starting point is a structural mismatch that is now being quantified. An SK Hynix research roadmap published in Nature Electronics puts hardware compute throughput growth at roughly 3x every two years, while interconnect bandwidth grows at only about 1.4x over the same period. The gap between these two rates widens continuously, forming what SK Hynix calls the bandwidth wall.

The physical basis is the energy ceiling of copper interconnect. Conventional copper cabling consumes over 10 pJ/bit. As AI cluster scale expands from thousands of GPUs to tens of thousands and transmission distance extends from in-rack to rack-to-rack, copper's power consumption and signal attenuation worsen in tandem. Beyond 200G, signal attenuation becomes severe after traversing longer copper paths through ABF substrates, PCBs, and connectors, pushing the industry toward shortened copper paths and elongated optical paths — moving the electro-optical conversion element ever closer to the ASIC to reduce power, latency, and signal loss.

Silicon photonics currently achieves 2.4 to 5 pJ/bit, versus 12 to 15 pJ/bit for 2024-era copper systems — a reduction of more than two-thirds. In thousand-GPU AI clusters, this efficiency differential translates into megawatt-level power differences, which is the direct driver behind CPO's transition from optional to necessary.

Three paths, one multiplicative effect
TSMC's three paths are not independent technology choices. They correspond to three distinct physical dimensions of optical interconnect, each with its own engineering constraints.

The first path — per-lane speed from 200G toward 400G — depends on modulator performance. TSMC Vice President Hsu Kuo-chin said on August 31 that COUPE will mass-produce the world's first single-channel 200 Gbps micro-ring modulator in 2026, with 400 Gbps modulators doubling that rate subsequently. The micro-ring modulator is critical because its footprint is far smaller than a conventional Mach-Zehnder modulator, making it suitable for high-density integration within a compact package; it has demonstrated a bit error rate below one in a billion.

The second path — channel count from 16 to 32, 64, and beyond — involves the density of the fiber array unit. FAU has been formally incorporated into the COUPE bandwidth expansion roadmap, shifting from a peripheral component to a core interface of the optical engine. Multi-row FAU adoption means the number of fibers integrated in a single fiber bundle multiplies, with corresponding increases in precision alignment requirements.

The third path — wavelength-division multiplexing — is the most systemically complex. It requires integrating multiple laser sources and modulators of different wavelengths within the same optical engine and ensuring wavelength selectivity at the demultiplexing end meets bit error rate requirements. TSMC's two strategies — "Fast and Narrow" raising per-lane speed, and "Slow and Wide" increasing channel density through WDM and multi-row FAU — are not mutually exclusive at the system level but combined according to application scenario.

The combined effect of all three advancing simultaneously — per-lane speed doubling times channel count doubling times wavelength count doubling — forms the mathematical basis for bandwidth doubling every two years. By 2030, TSMC plans to raise bandwidth density from 0.5 Tbps per millimeter to 4 Tbps, an eightfold increase in four years.

The yield multiplication: an engineering problem, not a manufacturing one
The technical feasibility of the bandwidth path is established. But the industrialization bottleneck sits at a more fundamental level.

CPO system yield is a multiplication problem, not an addition problem. Assume a CPO system integrates 32 optical engines — considering that each optical engine in Nvidia's Spectrum-X CPO switch contains 16 200G optical channels, high-end configurations require multiple engines in parallel. At an individual engine yield of 95%, the system integration yield equals 0.95 to the 32nd power, approximately 19%.

SemiAnalysis adopted this calculation logic in its June 2026 report "Powered Down, Lights Off," arriving at a system-level yield of about 19.4%, far below the threshold for scalable profitability. That calculation triggered a reassessment of CPO production timelines, with SemiAnalysis concluding that large-scale CPO production would be delayed to 2028 or 2029 — significantly behind prior market expectations. AAOI fell 17.17% that day, and Coherent dropped 11.44%.

An important qualification: the calculation assumes yield failures occur independently at each serial stage, meaning defective units from earlier stages are not screened out before entering the next stage. If front-end testing can effectively filter non-conforming units before optical engines enter system assembly, the yield base for subsequent assembly is 100% rather than 95%, and the system yield calculation changes materially. This dispute's substance is that CPO's core production bottleneck is not manufacturing itself but whether testing can perform defect screening at the right position, at acceptable cost and time.

Morgan Stanley's supply chain research identifies the improvement vector. Insertion 2 wafer-level testing — the first node that validates both electrical and optical signals simultaneously — has compressed from one wafer per day in the second half of 2025 to approximately six hours per wafer currently, with a target of three to four hours per wafer within the next six to twelve months. Testing efficiency directly determines front-end screening throughput, and front-end screening throughput determines whether the yield multiplication formula holds. Without testing efficiency gains, sufficient PIC capacity cannot translate into actual shipments.

TSMC is advancing wafer-level edge coupler testing, aiming to complete CP testing at the wafer stage and screen defective components before they enter expensive advanced packaging processes. The logic: perform as much defect screening as possible at the lowest-cost stage of packaging, avoiding resource waste when defective units enter subsequent high-cost steps.

Competitive landscape: differentiated positioning across three routes
TSMC's COUPE platform is not the only CPO path. Broadcom, Nvidia, Samsung, and Intel have each selected different technology routes and customer positioning.

Broadcom is the CPO production pioneer. Its 51.2T Bailly CPO switch has entered small-volume production, with Delta Electronics and Micas Networks assisting volume introduction, achieving up to 70% power reduction versus conventional pluggable optical transceivers, and having completed deployment validation with Meta and other hyperscalers.

Nvidia's CPO strategy reflects stronger vertical integration. The Spectrum-X CPO switch, using TSMC's COUPE packaging, entered full production in August 2026, covering Spectrum 6810 (102.4T) and Spectrum 6800 (409.6T), integrating second-generation 3.2T optical engines with 16 200G optical channels each. The switch achieves laser count reduction of 4x, power reduction of 5x, and MTBI improvement of 10x. Nvidia's distinctive approach is a unified photonics strategy — using the same optical hardware across Quantum, Spectrum, and NVLink switches to minimize manufacturing cost. In the Vera Rubin platform, Nvidia introduced CPO-based NVLink switches to create NVL576 (8-rack) pods, extending CPO from the network layer to the compute interconnect layer.

Samsung chose a foundry positioning rather than chip design. Its roadmap shows 2027 for thermocompression-bonded optical engines, 2028 for transition to hybrid bonding, and 2029 for turnkey CPO foundry service — customers provide designs, Samsung delivers chips, packaging, coupling, and testing. Samsung has secured optical communication orders and plans to begin large-scale production in the second half of 2026, while negotiating commercial cooperation with several major global customers.

Intel focuses on extending its EMIB-T packaging route into optical interconnect, leveraging its differentiated advanced packaging capability. At the foundry level, GlobalFoundries acquired Advanced Micro Foundry in November 2025, establishing what it claims is the largest pure-play silicon photonics foundry, expanding capacity and R&D in Singapore.

The structural implication of this competitive landscape is that the CPO value chain's profit pool distribution differs from the pluggable optical module era. In the pluggable era, value accrued primarily at the optical module packaging stage. In the CPO era, value shifts toward chip design (Broadcom, Nvidia), advanced packaging (TSMC), and system integration — compressing the bargaining power of traditional optical module packagers.

Capacity path and financial transmission
TSMC's capacity buildout provides a quantified industrialization path. Its PIC capacity expansion starts from roughly 500 wafers per month currently, reaching 10,000 per month in Q2 2026, 15,000 in Q4 2026, and exceeding 25,000 by 2028 — a more than 30x expansion in three years. Each wafer accommodates 648 dies, implying annual PIC output of up to 194 million units.

The loss from capacity to actual shipments is significant. At a 50% SoIC integration yield, 10,000 wafers per month can produce roughly 2 million optical engines, but downstream packaging losses may reduce actual shipments to approximately 390,000 units. Morgan Stanley projects global CPO switch shipments reaching approximately 23,000 units in 2026 — led by Nvidia's 100T switches — rising to 59,000 in 2027 and 200,000 by 2030. If yield continues improving, actual optical engine shipments corresponding to TSMC's 2027 PIC capacity could reach approximately 7.8 million units.

On customer adoption cadence, 2026–2027 is led by Nvidia, Broadcom, and AMD adopting TSMC's COUPE platform, followed by MediaTek, Marvell, and Ayar Labs expected to join the volume platform in 2028. This diffusion path means CPO will penetrate from flagship switch products into the broader ASIC and networking chip market.

TSMC's gross margin in the second half of 2026 may face erosion from initial 2nm production and overseas fab costs, but its leading-edge pricing power provides a hedge — 2nm wafer pricing is expected to approach $30,000, and price increases can effectively offset cost pressure. CPO as an incremental advanced packaging segment carries pricing logic similar to CoWoS: packaging value rises with chip complexity, and TSMC's pricing power in high-end packaging is not constrained by foundry capacity competition.

What to track
Three signals will determine whether the CPO bandwidth path translates from roadmap into verifiable industrial cadence.

Whether Insertion 2 test time compresses to three to four hours per wafer by 2027. Morgan Stanley identifies this metric as the core bottleneck converting CPO capacity into shipments. Test time directly determines front-end screening throughput, and screening efficiency determines whether the yield multiplication formula holds. Without compression, even ample PIC capacity cannot yield sufficient optical engine shipments.

The CPO adoption node in Nvidia's Feynman architecture. Nvidia's CPO roadmap extends from switch CPO in Blackwell, to NVLink CPO in Vera Rubin, to potential PIC-ASIC 3D vertical integration in Feynman. Supply chain surveys indicate CoPoS technology has been incorporated into Nvidia's Feynman GPU architecture blueprint, with the 2029 Feynman Ultra version expected to fully adopt the architecture. If Feynman's CPO adoption proceeds on schedule, CPO extends from the switching layer to the compute layer, materially expanding the addressable market.

Samsung's CPO foundry customer adoption cadence. Samsung plans to offer turnkey CPO foundry service in 2029, having already secured optical communication orders with large-scale production planned for the second half of 2026. If Samsung successfully onboards major customers between 2028 and 2029, it would pose a substantive challenge to TSMC's dominance in CPO foundry; if customer adoption lags, TSMC's COUPE platform will retain its first-mover advantage.

The CPO bandwidth path's regularity — doubling every two years — is physically feasible. Whether that regularity translates into industrial cadence depends on the coordinated evolution of three variables: test efficiency, yield engineering, and customer adoption. Bandwidth density improvement is a determined technical direction; manufacturability improvement is an uncertain engineering challenge. The time gap between the two is the key variable determining CPO's industrialization pace. TSMC has defined the slope of the bandwidth curve through three parallel paths, but whether that curve delivers on the roadmap's cadence depends on whether yield engineering — this division problem — can approach unity at every serial node.

At that point, the school is utterly worthless. No one will hire from it. So if you are a bright kid of any race, you *can't* go to El Paso. You're wasting your time. And chances are good that the classes you need are only offered once a year and fill up quick because they spend all their time offering remedial classes for the thousands of near illiterate students they have.

Understand that Texas could fill *all* of its UT campuses with kids scoring 1200 or higher on the SAT. All of them. So the notion that oh, it's ok that the lower schools admit incompetents is just bullshit.  But that's the story.

So no, a good kid can't now go to UTEP as a freshman. It's a billion times better to go to a community college for two years and transfer to a better campus when the diversity yutzes aren't counting.

text:
At 24, She Took Her Seat in the Cockpit of China’s Largest Transport Aircraft
24岁，她坐进了中国最大运输机的驾驶舱

Li Xueran, a post‑2000s female pilot, now serves as co‑pilot of the Y‑20, China’s large‑scale strategic transport aircraft.

Recruited into the military at 19, she reached the Y‑20 cockpit by age 24. Over five years, she transformed from an ordinary high‑school student into a large transport‑aircraft pilot. Her story is no legend of innate genius. Instead, it offers a genuine account of a Chinese Gen‑Z young person refining herself relentlessly under high‑pressure conditions to build professional competence step‑by‑step.

## A Spontaneous Application “Just for a Friend” Changed Her Life

Li Xueran had dreamed of joining the military since childhood, yet she never imagined she could become a pilot — it felt far beyond her reach.

In her senior year of high school, an Air Force pilot‑recruitment presentation came to her school. Teachers asked her and another female classmate to sit in on the session. Inspired by the briefing, her classmate resolved to apply. Li Xueran signed up merely to accompany her friend, viewing it as nothing more than a routine medical check‑up. Unexpectedly, she passed more than 100 screening tests one after another. By the secondary assessment stage, the thick stack of application forms had dwindled to a slim handful. At that moment, a thought crossed her mind: maybe I really can do this. In the end, she became the only female flight cadet admitted that year across the three northeastern provinces of China.

This detail merits attention: her admission was no token gesture, but the hard‑won outcome of fierce competition.

## First Lesson in Barracks: Romantic Fantasies Give Way to Extreme Training

Upon entering military camp, her romantic visions of flying quickly collided with harsh reality.

Physical conditioning, aviation theories and flight techniques daily pushed her physical and mental endurance to the limit. Training was designed not only to test one’s stamina, but also the ability to maintain precision under immense pressure.

Li Xueran later recalled that the most vital lesson she learned in those years was to manage fear, fatigue and self‑doubt. In aviation, even a tiny mistake could escalate into serious trouble. Cadets therefore had to drill complex procedures until they became instinctive reflexes.

## The Toughest Hurdle: Staying Calm When the Aircraft “Misbehaves”

Aerobatic flight training marked her most stressful period.

During aerial manoeuvres, instrument gauges fluctuated wildly while her body endured extreme g‑forces. Human instinct urges panic in such moments. Rather than relying on raw courage to push through, Li Xueran repeatedly rehearsed every sequence of movements, throttle adjustments and gaze shifts on the ground, until the whole routine turned into muscle memory.

On assessment day, she remained surprisingly composed while executing the manoeuvres. After landing, her palms were soaked in sweat, yet she felt an unprecedented sense of reassurance.

This was not confidence born of “never being afraid”, but confidence stemming from “being fully prepared”.

## A “Naturally‑Gifted Pilot”? She Questions the Label

Some people call Li Xueran a naturally‑gifted pilot, a label she does not fully embrace.

In her eyes, gifted peers abound around her. What truly matters is how one makes use of whatever talent they possess. Between 19 and 24, she dedicated herself almost entirely to one goal: earning her place beneath the blue sky.

This mindset is far from unique among Chinese Gen‑Z. A growing number of young people are stepping into high‑threshold fields including engineering, medicine, aviation and technology. They believe competence is not innate, but forged through consistent devotion.

## From Basic Trainer to Y‑20: Every Stage Means Starting Anew

Li Xueran graduated top of her class from basic trainer aircraft training. The outstanding result qualified her for further training, yet it brought no easy path ahead. She then transitioned to the Y‑7 transport aircraft, and after rounds of rigorous evaluations, qualified as co‑pilot for the Y‑20.

The Y‑20, codenamed “Kunpeng”, is China’s domestically‑developed large long‑range military transport aircraft. For young pilots, stepping into its cockpit means largely starting over: its systems are far more sophisticated, responsibilities heavier, and margins for error narrower.

Li Xueran shared that when she first entered the Y‑20 cockpit, the sea of dials and control sticks drove home a stark truth: all she had learned before laid only the foundation, and the real challenges were just beginning.

## A Contingent of Female Transport Pilots Averaging 22 Years Old

The unit of female transport pilots Li Xueran belongs to has an average age of merely 22.

This statistic illustrates that young Chinese pilots are entrusted with genuine operational responsibilities at an early stage. Far from remaining in the background as mere observers, they train for real‑world missions: operating complex systems, managing flight workflows, and undertaking transport and support assignments.

China has steadily expanded female participation in military aviation in recent years. Li Xueran’s story reflects a clear trend: young women are no longer rare exceptions in technical military roles, but are becoming the new normal of the younger generation.

This year marks the 10th anniversary of the official commissioning of the Y‑20 in Chinese military service. For Li Xueran, the milestone is more than a number. Her story could easily be simplified into a feel‑good inspirational tale, yet it deserves deeper reflection.

She embodies a cohort of young Chinese people: stepping early into highly demanding technical professions, embracing pressure as part of growth, and measuring themselves against professional standards rather than outside praise.

From that high‑school pilot‑recruitment briefing to her seat inside the strategic transport aircraft cockpit, Li Xueran’s journey is more than a personal achievement. It serves as a window showing how China’s younger generation is trained, tested, and empowered to take on roles once deemed out of reach.

    李雪冉，一位"00后"女飞行员，如今已是中国大型战略运输机运-20的副驾驶。
    从19岁招飞入伍到24岁飞上运-20，她用五年时间完成了从普通高中生到大型运输机飞行员的蜕变。她的故事不是"天赋异禀"的传奇，而是一个中国Z世代年轻人在高压环境中反复打磨自己、一步步走向专业的真实记录。

【一次"陪朋友试试"的报名，改变了人生方向】
    李雪冉从小想当兵，但从没想过自己能成为飞行员——那太遥远了。
    高三那年，空军招飞宣讲来到她的学校。老师安排她和另一位女同学去旁听。同学听完后热血沸腾，决心报考；李雪冉则是抱着"陪她试试，反正就当体检"的心态报了名。没想到，初选100多项检查，她一关一关闯了过来。到了复选阶段，报名表从厚厚一摞缩减为薄薄一小沓。那一刻，她心里冒出一个念头：也许我真的可以。最终，她成为那一年中国东北三省唯一被录取的女飞行学员。
    这个细节值得关注——她的入选不是象征性的，而是实打实竞争出来的结果。

【军营里的第一课：浪漫想象让位于极限训练】
    踏进军营后，关于飞行的浪漫想象很快被现实击碎。
    体能训练、航空理论、飞行技术，每一天都在挑战身体和意志的极限。训练的目的不仅是看谁能扛住，更是看谁能在高压下保持精准。
    李雪冉后来回忆说，那几年她学会的最重要的事，是如何控制恐惧、疲劳和自我怀疑。在航空领域，一个微小的失误可能演变为严重问题。因此，学员必须把复杂操作练成本能反应。

【最难的一关：当飞机"不听话"时保持冷静】
    学习特技飞行是她压力最大的阶段。
    空中翻转时，仪表盘数据剧烈跳动，身体承受异常过载，人的本能反应是慌张。李雪冉的应对方式不是靠勇气硬扛，而是在地面反复推演每一个动作衔接、油门配合、视线转移，直到整套流程变成肌肉记忆。
    考核那天，真正做起动作时她反而异常平静。落地后手心全是汗，但心里有一种从未有过的踏实感。
    那不是"从没害怕过"的自信，而是"已经准备好了"的自信。

【"天赋型选手"？她不完全认同这个标签】
    有人称李雪冉是"天赋型选手"。她自己并不完全接受。
    在她看来，身边最不缺的就是有天赋的人。真正重要的是你怎么对待天赋。从19岁到24岁，她几乎只做了一件事：让自己配得上头顶那片蓝天。
    这种心态在中国Z世代中并不罕见。越来越多年轻人进入工程、医学、航空、科技等高门槛领域，他们相信能力不是天生的，而是靠持续投入换来的。

【从初教机到运-20：每一步都是重新开始】
    初教机结业，李雪冉综合排名第一。这个成绩帮她拿到了继续前进的资格，但并没有让下一步变得轻松。她随后改装运-7，又通过层层考核，最终成为运-20的副驾驶。
    运-20是中国自主研发的大型远程军用运输机，代号"鲲鹏"。对于年轻飞行员来说，进入它的驾驶舱意味着在很多方面从头学起——系统更复杂，责任更重大，容错空间更小。
    李雪冉说，第一次走进运-20驾驶舱时，满眼的仪表和操纵杆让她立刻明白：之前学到的一切只是基础，真正的考验才刚刚开始。

【一群平均年龄22岁的女运输机飞行员】
    李雪冉所在的女运输机飞行员队伍，平均年龄只有22岁。
    这个细节说明，中国的年轻飞行员正在被快速赋予实际责任。她们不是待在后方"见习"，而是在为执行真实任务做准备——操作复杂系统、管理飞行流程、承担运输保障任务。
    中国近年来持续扩大女性在军事航空领域的参与。李雪冉的故事折射出一个趋势：年轻女性在技术型军事岗位中不再是罕见的例外，而是正在成为新一代的常态。
    今年是中国运-20正式列装十周年。对李雪冉来说，这个节点不只是数字。她的故事很容易被包装成一个简单的励志叙事。但它比那更值得关注。
    她代表着一批中国年轻人：很早就进入高要求的技术领域，把压力视为成长的一部分，用专业标准而非外界评价来衡量自己。
    从高中招飞宣讲到坐上战略运输机的驾驶舱，李雪冉的经历不只是个人成就，更是一扇窗口——让人看到中国年轻一代如何被训练、被考验、被推向曾经看似遥不可及的岗位。
